person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Speakers tend to repeat the syntactic forms of sentences in subsequent utterances that are minimally related in lexical, conceptual, or discourse content.

span.label: syntactic persistence in language production
span.quote: This involves the repetition of syntactic forms across successive utterances.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: All of the experiments employed a syntactic priming paradigm that created a controlled analog of the situations that have revealed syntactic repetition in natural speech.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: syntactic (structural) priming: producing or hearing a sentence structure makes speakers more likely to reuse that same structure in a later, content-unrelated utterance - so syntax is represented and primed independently of meaning
span.quote: Speakers tend to repeat the syntactic forms of sentences in subsequent utterances that are minimally related in lexical, conceptual, or discourse content

span.label: it is unclear whether syntactic intrusions/perseverations can be accounted for in the same way
span.quote: In the case of syntactic intrusions or perseverations, however, it is not clear that the effects can be accounted for in a comparable way.

span.label: The null effect of the agency manipulation carries the usual indeterminacy of null results and may reflect a weak manipulation.
span.quote: The absence of an agency effect creates the usual indeterminacy associated with null results, leaving open the possibility that message factors may have had a less consistent impact than syntactic factors because the agency manipulation was weak.

span.label: The symmetry between syntactic and conceptual matching rests on unreliable differences and a very small item sample.
span.quote: But because the differences were unreliable and based on a very limited sample of items, this symmetry should be treated cautiously.

span.label: Both lines of evidence for the isolability of syntactic processing are described by the author as tentative.
span.quote: Two types of evidence for such isolability were found, although both must be regarded as tentative.

span.label: extends → activation-based theories of language production
span.quote: The advantage of the syntactic activation hypothesis is that it provides a unitary explanation for phenomena that otherwise seem quite disparate.

span.label: builds-on → the competition model of Bates and MacWhinney (1982; MacWhinney, Bates, & Kliegl, 1984)
span.quote: This view of linguistic rules as graded rather than fully determinate is comparable to that incorporated into the competition model of Bates and MacWhinney (1982; MacWhinney, Bates, & Kliegl, 1984).

span.label: extends → Levelt and Kelter (1982) and Weiner and Labov (1983) on repetition of syntactic form in natural speech
span.quote: A parsimonious explanation of these results, and those of previous investigations (Levelt & Kelter, 1982; Weiner & Labov, 1983), is that the production of sentences results in the activation or strengthening of the syntactic rules or procedures involved in their creation.

span.label: replicates → Experiment 2 of this paper
span.quote: The results thus replicated those of Experiment 2, but with a different cover task that encouraged fuller processing of the primes.
